title: SIEM outbound pipeline: design notes, connector patterns, and customer readiness checklist
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note captures a pragmatic outbound pipeline design for SIEM exports (Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs API, Microsoft Sentinel / Event Hub ingestion), plus customer-facing readiness checklist and connector-level configuration guidance. It focuses on delivery guarantees, schema evolution, RBAC v2 implications, and evidence automation hooks.

Audience:
- Eng: infra/serving-runtime, private-deploy teams
- Security & compliance owners
- Solutions / customer success when onboarding SIEM integrations

High-level goals:
- Provide delivery patterns that meet most customer requirements: near-real-time (<30s median), at-least-once delivery, observable (DLQ/metrics), and privacy-preserving (PII redaction configurable).
- Support multiple transport modes: direct HTTP (HEC / Datadog), Event Hub / Kafka buffered forwarder, and S3 archival as fallback for bulk delivery.
- Keep schema stable while allowing additive evolution; provide a clear compatibility story for customers.

Key design components (summary):
1) Event schema & audit envelope
   - All exports use a single audit envelope with these canonical fields (mandatory):
     - timestamp (RFC3339 UTC)
     - tenant_id (string)
     - product (string) e.g., "hosted-api", "dedicated"
     - event_type (string) e.g., "model.generate.request", "role.change", "audit.login"
     - request_id (UUID)",
     - actor (object encoded as JSON string) -> minimal: {"id":"u-123","type":"user|service"} (stringified in small footprints)
     - outcome (string): success|failure|partial
     - ip_address (string) optional
     - trace_id (string) optional for correlating with traces
     - payload (object encoded as JSON string) -- operation-specific details (size-limited)

   - Rationale: single envelope simplifies field mapping for Splunk/Datadog and avoids map fragmentation. Payload remains opaque for customers who prefer to parse on their side.

   - Sample (NDJSON line):
   {\"timestamp\":\"2026-03-10T14:22:09Z\",\"tenant_id\":\"t-87a12\",\"product\":\"hosted-api\",\"event_type\":\"model.generate.request\",\"request_id\":\"b7b6d2f4-9c3a-4bb0-8e1d-e4a2f3d5c6a7\",\"actor\":\"{\\\"id\\\":\\\"u-901\\\",\\\"type\\\":\\\"user\\\"}\",\"outcome\":\"success\",\"trace_id\":\"trace-1a2b3c\",\"payload\":\"{\\\"prompt_tokens\\\":23,\\\"resp_tokens\\\":141,\\\"model\\\":\\\"rwd-v1\\\"}\" }

2) Transport modes and recommended configs
   - Direct HTTP (Splunk HEC / Datadog Logs API):
     - Use token-based auth (HEC token, Datadog API key). Recommend dedicated token per-tenant or per-organization for auditability.
     - Batch size: 50-500 events per request depending on average event size (target 256KB payloads).
     - Retries: exponential backoff with jitter (max attempts 8), respect 429 Retry-After.
     - TLS: require TLS1.2+ (prefer TLS1.3), client cert optional for high-security customers.

   - Event Hub / Kafka forwarder (recommended for high-throughput or private deployments):
     - Use partitioning key = tenant_id to keep ordering per tenant when needed.
     - Buffering policy: commit to local durable queue -> flush to broker every 500ms or when 2MB reached.
     - Compression: gzip at producer.
     - Consumer contract: downstream connector instances read from Event Hub and push to destination with retries/backoff + DLQ to S3.
     - Benefits: decouples spikes, supports guaranteed-at-least-once, better for on-prem customers behind firewall.

   - S3 archival + pull connector:
     - Periodic (1–15m) batch uploads in NDJSON gzip to a customer-owned S3 (or redwood-managed) as a fallback for bulk transfers or air-gapped scenarios.

3) Authentication & RBAC v2 considerations
   - We must align tokens and roles with RBAC v2: create a mapping between RBAC roles and export tokens/permissions. Example: "audit-exporter" role can read only audit indices for tenant scope.
   - Tokens used by connectors should be scoped and rotated automatically via KMS integration. Rotation window: 30–90 days.
   - Logging of token usage must appear in the audit log itself (token_id, action=export.push).

4) Schema evolution & versioning
   - Envelope includes a schema_version field (semantic minor) - default v1.0.
   - We support additive evolution only: new top-level optional keys allowed; do not rename/remove fields without a deprecation period (90 days).
   - Provide a "schema diff" endpoint (internal) + published change log for customers.

5) Privacy & evidence automation hooks
   - PII redaction: configuration per-tenant with three modes: allow, mask, drop. Redaction applied before export.
   - Evidence automation: for compliance customers we support an "evidence" tag in the envelope that triggers retention snapshots (write a copy to immutably-versioned S3 bucket and create a compliance record).
   - Audit trail for evidence: record the snapshot_id, retention_window, and justification in the export envelope and in Redwood internal audit DB.

6) Observability and operational controls
   - Must emit the following metrics per-export-pipeline: events_sent, events_failed, avg_latency_ms, batch_size_distribution, consumer_lag (for Kafka/EventHub).
   - DLQ policy: after N transient failures (configurable, default 8), event moves to encrypted DLQ S3 with metadata and retry ticket.

7) Customer onboarding & readiness checklist (copyable for Solutions/CS)
   - Network: provide egress IP ranges (CIDR list) and FQDNs for Splunk/Datadog/Sentinel endpoints; confirm firewall rules allow outbound HTTPS and/or Event Hub ports.
   - Auth: exchange destination token/endpoint details; decide whether customer will provide tenant-scoped tokens or we will issue delegate tokens.
   - Schema: confirm which event_types customer wants (audit-only vs full payloads) and PII redaction mode.
   - Volume: estimate peak eps (events/sec) and average event size; choose transport (direct vs Event Hub) accordingly.
   - SLOs & retention: agree on delivery SLO (e.g., 99.9% delivery within 1 minute) and data retention requirements for evidence mode.
   - Test plan: run smoke test (send 1000 events), validate mapping, verify DLQ behavior by injecting a mock 500 response.
   - Compliance: sign off on legal egress if cross-border logs will be sent; if not allowed use S3-batch export into customer-controlled bucket.

Connector-level specs (quick reference)
 - Splunk HEC: endpoint: https://{splunk-host}:8088/services/collector/event
   - auth: HEC token (X-Splunk-Token header)
   - recommended content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
   - batch mode: NDJSON lines in body
   - success codes: 200; 5xx -> retry, 429 -> honor Retry-After header
\ - Datadog Logs API: endpoint: https://http-intake.logs.datadoghq.com/v1/input
   - auth: api key in URL path or DD-API-KEY header; use default ingestion endpoints per region
   - batching: JSON array of events or ndjson; prefer ndjson to reduce parsing overhead
\ - Microsoft Sentinel (via Event Hub):
   - for Hosted/Private: publish to Event Hub namespace; customer sets up Diagnostic Setting to ingest from Event Hub into Sentinel if needed
   - auth: SAS token or AAD service principal; recommend AAD for long-term integration
\Non-functional/operational notes and tradeoffs
 - At-least-once vs exactly-once: we choose at-least-once for simplicity; customers who need dedupe should use request_id and idempotency at ingestion side.
 - Latency vs cost: batching reduces cost but increases tail-latency; provide per-tenant policy knobs in Console (target latency percentiles and max batch size).
 - Throttling: global and per-tenant throttles; upstream rate limit (429) handling includes exponential backoff and fallback to S3/archive if sustained.
\Open questions / TODOs:
 - Do we want to provide an "event-transform-as-a-service" shim so customers can request per-tenant field-mapping transforms in-console (UX effort)?
 - RBAC mapping: finalize role->token mapping with identity team (PR open: github.com/redwood-inference/identity/pull/129).
 - Retention / legal hold API for evidence-snapshots needs spec from legal (ticket: JIRA-LEGAL-88).
\Appendix: quick troubleshooting guide for Solutions engineers
 - If customer sees missing events: check DLQ for stalled items, confirm token scopes, verify firewall allowing egress, check producer metrics for queue saturation.
 - If customer sees duplicates: ask them to dedupe on request_id or set consumer side dedupe windows.
 - If schema mismatch: enable schema_version header in logs and send a sample failing event to engineering with captured raw payload.
\Notes to self: prioritize a lightweight test harness that can be run by CS (python script) to push sample NDJSON to Splunk/Datadog and validate mapping. Put that under infra-telemetry/test-harness repo.

End of notes.

(contains rough drafts, TODOs, and customer-checklist copy — use as working doc for SRE + Solutions onboarding)
